title: Deligne–Laumon affine-line estimate for the middle extension
statement:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$ ([def-weil-punctual-weights]) and
unramified at infinity. Then, for the ordinary middle extension
$j_*\mathcal F$ of [def-wf-middle-extension] and the compactly
supported cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], for
every integer $r$

$$
H_c^r(A,j_*\mathcal F)\quad\text{has weights at most }w+r
$$

in the sense of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. More precisely,
$H_c^0(A,j_*\mathcal F)=0$, $H_c^2(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ is $\iota$-pure of
weight $w+2$ (possibly zero), $H_c^r(A,j_*\mathcal F)=0$ for
$r\notin\{0,1,2\}$, and $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F)$ has weights at most
$w+1$.

proof.text: The affine line $A_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0[t]$ is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve. Apply [lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints] to the given dense open $j$ and pure lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$. It gives $H_c^0(A,j_*\mathcal F)=0$, $H_c^r(A,j_*\mathcal F)=0$ for $r\notin\{0,1,2\}$, and purity of weight $w+2$ in degree two. A pure Frobenius module of weight $w+2$ has a one-step filtration exhibiting weights at most $w+2$ by [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]; a zero module has the empty filtration and satisfies every upper bound. Thus only degree one remains.

For a finite constant extension $k'_0=\mathbf F_{q^m}$, use the same algebraic closure $k$. Then $(U_0\times_{k_0}k'_0)\times_{k'_0}k=U$ and likewise the geometric affine line is still $A$. Restricting the Weil structure to this extension retains the underlying sheaf and replaces its Frobenius isomorphism by its $m$-fold composite: [lem-wf-weil-group-constant-extension] identifies the new degree-one element with $s^m$. By [def-weil-frobenius-detailed] the semilinear geometric map is $g_A^m$, not the absolute Frobenius. The underlying open $j:U\hookrightarrow A$ and the section formula for its ordinary direct image [def-wf-middle-extension] are identical, so the underlying $j_*\mathcal F$ is identical. Functoriality on the composite Weil isomorphism, using [prop-weil-operations] and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], makes its cohomology operator $F^m$. Local Frobenius at a point of residue degree $e$ over $x$ is $F_x^e$, with norm $q_x^e$, so punctual purity retains weight $w$. The geometric inertia group at infinity and its action are unchanged, so unramifiedness is retained. We will descend the bound after working over this extension.

Apply [lem-zl-geometric-constituents-any-base] to $\mathcal F$ on $U_0$, which is smooth and geometrically connected over $k_0$ (a dense open of the geometrically integral line). After one finite constant extension, harmless by Step 2, there is a filtration $0=\mathcal F^0\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F^n=\mathcal F$ by lisse Weil subsheaves; remove repeated terms, so the quotients $\mathcal M_i=\mathcal F^i/\mathcal F^{i-1}$ are nonzero, lisse and geometrically irreducible. (The blueprint's geometric-constituent lemma of this unit states only a filtration by Weil subsheaves; Step 4 needs lisse terms.) At a closed point $x$ the stalks give short exact sequences of local Frobenius modules $0\to\mathcal F^i_{\bar x}\to\mathcal F_{\bar x}\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal F^i)_{\bar x}\to0$ and $0\to\mathcal F^{i-1}_{\bar x}\to\mathcal F^i_{\bar x}\to\mathcal M_{i,\bar x}\to0$, so [lem-a1-spectrum-exact-sequence] puts the eigenvalues on $\mathcal F^i_{\bar x}$ and on $\mathcal M_{i,\bar x}$ among those on $\mathcal F_{\bar x}$: every $\mathcal F^i$ and $\mathcal M_i$ is punctually pure of weight $w$. In the fundamental representation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation], inertia at infinity acts trivially on the original generic stalk, hence also on every subspace and quotient. Thus each $\mathcal M_i$ is unramified at infinity. A Weil-stable subspace is in particular geometrically stable, so geometric irreducibility implies irreducibility as a lisse Weil sheaf, with the meaning fixed in [rem-dl-a1-conventions].

For each $1\le i\le n$, the sequence $0\to\mathcal F^{i-1}\to\mathcal F^i\to\mathcal M_i\to0$ is short exact in lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves. By Step 3 its outer terms $\mathcal F^{i-1}$ and $\mathcal M_i$ are punctually pure of the same weight $w$ (including the zero first term). The base $A_0$ is smooth of relative dimension one. The dense open $U_0\subset A_0$ is quasi-compact: its closed complement is $V(f)$ for a nonzero polynomial $f\in k_0[t]$, so $U_0=D(f)$ is affine; if the complement is empty take $f=1$. Thus the current statement of [p-dl-a1-exact] applies with $C_0=A_0$ and $Z_0=A_0\setminus U_0$, giving the exact sequence $0\to j_*\mathcal F^{i-1}\to j_*\mathcal F^i\to j_*\mathcal M_i\to0$ of Weil sheaves. This invocation uses the outer-term purity hypotheses of the current node.

source.place: Step 3: exactness of ordinary middle extension

proof.text: Forget the Weil structures in this short exact sequence. By [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible] (with $C_0=A_0$) the terms are objects of the constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], with their induced Weil structures. Clause 4 of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] produces a distinguished triangle in the underlying $D^b_c(A,\Qlb)$. Apply the exact compact-support operation for $a_A:A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose Weil lift is [prop-weil-operations], and then clause 5 of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. By the definition [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], this yields an exact triple $V_{i-1}\xrightarrow{a_i}V_i\xrightarrow{b_i}W_i$, where $V_i=H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F^i)$ and $W_i=H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M_i)$. Both arrows commute with Frobenius because the original sheaf arrows are Weil morphisms and compact-support cohomology is functorial on them. We require neither a triangulated structure on the category of Weil pairs nor a choice of a Weil-equivariant cone: exactness comes from the underlying triangle and equivariance of these two arrows comes from functoriality.

Fix one graded piece $\mathcal M$. If it is geometrically constant, its geometric representation is both trivial and irreducible, so any line is stable and its rank must be one. Its Weil action is therefore given by one scalar $b\ne0$ raised to the degree, namely the constant Weil twist [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], using the representation [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Apply [lem-a1-exceptional-constituents] to this rank-one constant sheaf on $U_0$ (without an Artin–Schreier factor). Its $H_c^1(U,\mathcal M)$ has weights at most $w+1$. The boundary sequence [prop-a1-curve-boundary-sequence] gives a surjection $g$ from this module onto $H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal M)$; its statement does not assert Frobenius compatibility. By that statement $g$ is induced by the first arrow $j_!j^*(j_*\mathcal M)\to j_*\mathcal M$ of the open–closed triangle, where $j^*j_*\mathcal M=\mathcal M$ by the section formula of [def-wf-middle-extension]. Here $A$, $U$, $Z$ come from $k_0$ and $j_*\mathcal M$ is a constructible Weil sheaf by [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible], so this arrow is Weil-equivariant by the last clause of [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages]. Compact-support direct image and the composition isomorphism $R(a_Aj)_!\simeq Ra_{A!}j_!$ are morphisms of Weil complexes by [prop-weil-operations]. Hence $g$ commutes with Frobenius. The quotient bound [lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds] gives the required bound for $W_i$. This uses the statement of the exceptional-constituents node, rather than the computation inside its proof.

Choose a nontrivial additive character $\psi$ of the current finite constant field, in the sense of [def-fd-additive-character]. Such a choice is elementary: choose a nonzero $\mathbf F_p$-linear functional $L:k'_0\to\mathbf F_p$ and a nontrivial $p$-th root of unity $\zeta\in\Qlb$, and put $\psi(x)=\zeta^{L(x)}$. The functional is surjective; since $p$ is prime and $\Qlb$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, $\zeta$ has order $p$. Hence this is a nontrivial homomorphism. If $\mathcal M$ is not geometrically constant, its nonzero irreducible lisse status and unramifiedness at infinity satisfy [lem-a1-unramified-nonexceptional] for this $\psi$. It is therefore constituent-nonexceptional, including exclusion of the trivial constituent at $a=0$. Apply the current [cor-a1-fourier-middle-hc1] directly with this character: $j$ is dense in the affine line, $\mathcal M$ is irreducible lisse, punctually pure of weight $w$, and constituent-nonexceptional. Its conclusion is the bound $w+1$ for $W_i$.

Induct on $i$ in the filtration. The initial term is $V_0=H_c^1(A,j_*0)=0$, so the bound holds by the empty filtration. Suppose it holds for $V_{i-1}$. In the exact triple of Step 5 set $I_i=\operatorname{im}a_i$ and $J_i=\operatorname{im}b_i$. These are Frobenius-stable, and $0\to I_i\to V_i\to J_i\to0$ is exact: its kernel is $\ker b_i=\operatorname{im}a_i$. The module $I_i$ is a quotient of $V_{i-1}$, while $J_i$ is a submodule of $W_i$. Steps 6–7 bound $W_i$ by $w+1$; [lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds] bounds $I_i$ and $J_i$, and [lem-a1-extension-bounds] bounds their extension $V_i$. Thus the bound holds for $V_n$ over $k'_0$. The argument allows nonsplit sequences and does not assume semisimplicity.

Return to the original field and put $V=H_c^1(A,j_*\mathcal F)$, with its original Frobenius $F$. Step 2 identifies the module bounded in Step 8 with $(V,F^m)$ over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$. A mixed filtration of this module has pure quotients of weights $b_j\le w+1$. Successive application of [lem-a1-spectrum-exact-sequence] shows that each eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $F^m$ belongs to a quotient and satisfies $|\iota\lambda|^2=(q^m)^{b_j}\le(q^m)^{w+1}$. Apply [lem-a1-weight-bound-constant-extension] with $b=w+1$. Each eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F$ then satisfies $|\iota\alpha|^2\le q^{w+1}$, equivalently $|\iota\alpha|\le q^{(w+1)/2}$ since both sides are nonnegative. The statement [lem-a1-punctual-bound-module-mixed] turns this bound into mixedness of weights at most $w+1$ in the precise filtration sense of the theorem. Together with Step 1 this proves all the assertions, including the case $\mathcal F=0$ (an empty filtration).
